product-plan.title: Product Plan
product-plan.template:
# Product Plan template

Proposed planning format, not an official Codelit import schema. Omit irrelevant sections.

**Outcome:** [observable user result]
**Status:** Draft / Reviewed / Approved / Superseded
**Sources:** [actual source and revision, or not supplied]
**Owner:** [provided owner or unassigned]
**Assumptions:** [explicit, testable]

## User and problem

Who experiences the problem? What are they trying to accomplish? What evidence was supplied? What is still untested?

## First-release journey

[Starting state] -> [user action] -> [system result] -> [user value].

Include: [small first release].
Exclude: [deliberate boundaries].

## Requirements

| ID | User need | Priority | Acceptance check | Owner | Dependency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P-01 | [specific outcome] | Must/Should/Later | Given/When/Then | Unassigned | None/ID |

## Experience and state

Describe the necessary screens and normal, loading, empty, error, denied-access, and recovery states. Include keyboard use and relevant accessibility acceptance checks.

## Success and risk

| Measure | Why it matters | How measured | Baseline | Target status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [name] | [reason] | [observable event] | Unknown unless supplied | Proposed or supplied |

Highest-risk assumption: [assumption].
Small validation step: [test].
Delivery sequence: [thin slice, verify, bounded release].
Next decision: [one consequential unresolved item].

architecture.title: System Architecture
architecture.template:
# Architecture template

Reference design unless supported by actual code/configuration evidence. Component IDs are proposed labels, not repository paths.

## Decision and scope

Recommended shape: [design].
Reason: [user outcome and tradeoff].
Existing verified system: [evidence or unknown].
Proposed changes: [explicit boundary].

## Request path

Explain one request in ordinary language. Name who validates, who stores durable state, who approves a side effect, and who confirms its outcome.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[User] --> I[C-01 Interface]
  I --> O[C-02 Coordination]
  O --> W[C-03 Work execution]
  O <--> D[(C-04 Durable state)]
  W --> V[Validate proposed result]
  V --> H{Approval needed?}
  H -->|Yes| A[Authorized human approval]
  A --> E[Authorized external action]
  H -->|No side effect| R[Return draft]
  E --> P[Confirm provider outcome]
```

This is an illustrative diagram. Remove coordination, workers, or external actions when the scenario does not need them. Do not depict this as Codelit's actual implementation.

## Components and contracts

| ID | Responsibility | Inputs/outputs | State owner | Access boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 | [job] | [contract] | [owner or no storage] | [identity/scope] |

## Failure behavior

| Failure | Detection | Preserved state | Recovery | Proof needed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [failure] | [signal] | [checkpoint] | [safe next step] | [observed evidence] |

For relevant side effects, cover duplicate delivery, approval expiry, changed payload, cancellation, and a provider timeout after possible completion. Define idempotency scope without promising unsupported exactly-once effects.

## Decisions and verification

Explain the preferred design and one meaningful alternative. Identify tenant isolation, secrets handling, validation, logging/redaction, and retention decisions required by the use case. Mark unknown policies as unknown.

Link P-requirements to C-components and T-tests. Identify actual versus proposed test commands. Describe rollout and rollback or compensating action, plus evidence still needed before release.

agent-team.title: Supervised Agent Team
agent-team.template:
# Agent Team contract template

Proposed format only. A completed template is not a deployed team, a Codelit-native import, or proof of independent agent execution.

**Outcome:** [done condition]
**Mode:** Design-only / Simulated example / Observed execution
**Source:** [authorized input or not supplied]
**Destination:** [draft in chat by default]
**Trigger:** [manual by default; a proposed schedule is not enabled]
**Human owner:** [assigned or unassigned]

## Smallest useful roster

| ID | One responsibility | Inputs | Allowed tools/resources | Output contract | Check | Stop/escalate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-01 | [specific job] | [trusted/untrusted boundary] | [exact scope or none] | [fields] | [criteria] | [owner/condition] |

State why each added specialist is necessary. Keep deterministic validators and humans outside the agent roster.

## Workflow

| Step | Actor | Input -> output | Continuation | Stop condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [agent/code/human] | [contract] | [check] | [failure] |

## Side-effect approval

Exact proposed payload: [preview].
Destination and scope: [specific resource].
Authority: [authorized approver].
Approval binding: [content/version and target].
Expiry: [policy or unresolved].
Changed payload/destination: review again.
Execution authorization: enforce at provider boundary.
Evidence of completion: [tool result or observed stored effect].

## Operational bounds and durable state

Use only needed fields: workflow version, source revision, step, draft output, evidence references, approval record, attempts, deadline, budget, cancellation flag, provider operation ID, and confirmed/failed/unknown outcome. Do not fill unknown live IDs with realistic-looking samples.

Limits must be supplied or clearly proposed. Describe bounded retries, deduplication, restart, rejection, missing data, injection handling, invalid output, partial failure, unknown write outcome, and human escalation as relevant.

## Evaluation

| Test | Input/condition | Expected result | Evidence | Actual status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-01 | [condition] | [observable result] | [needed artifact] | Not run |

plan-and-ship.title: Connected Implementation Handoff
plan-and-ship.template:
# Connected engineering handoff

Proposed delivery format, not Codelit's official repo-pack schema.

## Source snapshot

Goal: [observable outcome].
Sources and revisions: [actual references or missing].
Accepted decisions: [actual accepted decisions].
Proposed changes: [new decisions awaiting review].
Evidence status: [none/sample/observed run, with source].

## Traceability

| Requirement | Component | Agent/human owner | Task | Acceptance test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P-01 | C-01 | A-01 or human | W-01 | T-01 |

Use only real identifiers from the current plan. Each important requirement needs an owner and test; unanswered assignment remains explicit rather than fabricated.

## Scoped implementation prompt

```text
Goal:
[observable user outcome]

Grounded context:
[verified repository/revision, documents, decisions, and relevant paths]

Included changes:
[bounded scope]

Excluded changes:
[explicit boundaries]

Constraints:
[existing conventions, data protection, compatibility, approval boundaries]

Ordered tasks:
[work items and dependencies]

Acceptance checks:
[user-visible checks, automated tests, failure/recovery cases]

Release and recovery:
[review gate, bounded rollout, rollback or compensating action]

Reporting:
Report actual changed files, commands run, observed results, unresolved issues,
and actions not performed. Do not claim tests, deployments, external writes,
or independent agent runs succeeded without observed evidence.
```

## Completion ledger

| Item | Status | Evidence | Remaining owner/action |
|---|---|---|---|
| [artifact/test/action] | Draft/Reviewed/Approved/Attempted/Confirmed/Failed/Unknown | [actual reference or none] | [next action] |

End with one concrete next action. Do not silently overwrite accepted work or imply that the handoff executed itself.
